task: Make isolated release-unit successor reevaluation resolve the exact locked dependency graph required by trusted semantic Plan/Atlas validation, while remaining fail-closed and preserving token/authority isolation.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded multi-unit rehearsal run 37566854069 / job 112629917634 correctly entered fresh release-unit reevaluation after main advanced to fb436df11ae3dbc7c348e50fbc656e18a94f83cf, but the isolated reevaluation worktree could not resolve the trusted repository dependency graph. Plan/Atlas loading failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for typescript, persisting U01 as STALE with RELEASE_UNIT_SUCCESSOR_REEVALUATION_BLOCK.
observableOutcomes: Reevaluation prepares a deterministic locked dependency environment before invoking shoperation-plan-before-code.mjs.
Dependency preparation is bound to the candidate worktree package-lock/package manifests and fails closed on install/preparation failure.
Proof subprocesses continue to receive empty GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN and gain no repository mutation authority.
Semantic Plan/Atlas reevaluation still runs against the exact candidate head and fresh current-main base.
A real reevaluation semantic failure still returns RELEASE_UNIT_SUCCESSOR_REEVALUATION_BLOCK rather than being reinterpreted as executable.
unresolvedRisks: A candidate dependency manifest change could make reuse of the trusted root node_modules stale.
Installing dependencies with lifecycle scripts could grant unnecessary execution surface inside a proof-only worktree.
Network/package-registry failure must not silently downgrade semantic validation.
Dependency setup must precede Plan/Atlas execution and must not modify repository-controlled tracked files.

in: Add deterministic locked dependency bootstrap to release-unit reevaluation before semantic Plan/Atlas validation.
Use npm ci with the candidate worktree lockfile and no audit/fund; suppress package lifecycle scripts for this proof-only environment unless a proven repository requirement says otherwise.
Preserve GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN scrubbing for dependency and proof subprocesses.
Add regression coverage for dependency-bootstrap ordering, token scrubbing, and fail-closed reevaluation behavior.
out: No bypass of successor reevaluation or Atlas/Plan authority.
No manual clearing of persisted STALE state.
No manual child PR creation, receipt fabrication, or release-state edits.
No storefront, database, deployment, template, Builder, payment, inventory, authentication or product-runtime changes.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This code runs inside the trusted write-capable release executor immediately before successor authorization. Environment completeness must be restored without weakening exact-head proof, authority isolation, or fail-closed behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Reevaluation dependency bootstrap occurs after candidate worktree creation and before shoperation-plan-before-code.mjs.
The bootstrap uses the candidate worktree locked dependency graph and fails closed on non-zero exit.
GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN remain scrubbed for bootstrap and semantic proof subprocesses.
Regression proof verifies bootstrap ordering and that a bootstrap failure returns RELEASE_UNIT_SUCCESSOR_REEVALUATION_BLOCK.
Exact-head CI passes all canonical guards, Completion Truth becomes VERIFIED, Lifecycle closes, then the fix is merged and the unchanged rehearsal is replayed from persisted state.
invariants: No trusted semantic proof is executed in an environment missing its declared locked dependencies.
No write credential is exposed to dependency/bootstrap or semantic proof subprocesses.
No dependency bootstrap failure is ignored.
Candidate head/base identity and successor reconciliation semantics remain unchanged.
Persisted release-state is advanced only through the existing CAS/event path.

failureModes: Temporary worktree lacks node_modules and Atlas cannot import typescript.
Locked dependency installation fails or registry is unavailable.
Candidate package-lock differs from trusted root dependencies.
Proof subprocess accidentally inherits write-capable GitHub credentials.
Dependency setup succeeds but semantic reevaluation legitimately blocks.
edgeCases: Candidate does not change package manifests.
npm ci exits non-zero before Plan execution.
Plan/Atlas exits non-zero after successful dependency bootstrap.
Temporary worktree cleanup runs after either success or failure.

alternatives.summary: Install exact candidate dependencies in the isolated reevaluation worktree with npm ci and token scrubbing.
alternatives.reason: Uses the candidate lockfile, avoids stale root dependency reuse, and fails closed if the exact proof environment cannot be established.

alternatives.summary: Link trusted executor root node_modules into the candidate worktree.
alternatives.reason: Could be stale when package manifests change and would make candidate dependency identity implicit rather than exact.

alternatives.summary: Reuse prior source admission evidence instead of running semantic reevaluation.
alternatives.reason: Would bypass fresh successor reconciliation and invalidate release authority.

alternatives.summary: Clear STALE state and continue the rehearsal manually.
alternatives.reason: Would fabricate authoritative execution progress and invalidate the rehearsal.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing edge is environment bootstrap inside an isolated reevaluation workspace, not missing release logic.
specialistReviews.resolution: Prepare exact candidate locked dependencies before semantic reevaluation.

specialistReviews.finding: Installing dependencies inside a write-capable executor can unnecessarily expose credentials or lifecycle-script execution.
specialistReviews.resolution: Scrub GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN and use proof-only npm ci with lifecycle scripts disabled; fail closed if this environment cannot be prepared.

specialistReviews.finding: Fresh successor reevaluation must remain exact-base and exact-candidate before authorization.
specialistReviews.resolution: Change only environment preparation; retain existing reconcile, Plan/Atlas and event/CAS semantics.

specialistReviews.finding: Live rehearsal exposed a dependency-resolution gap that unit mocks did not exercise.
specialistReviews.resolution: Lock bootstrap ordering/failure semantics with regression tests and replay the same persisted rehearsal state after merge.

challenge.finding: Semantic Atlas import fails before authoritative reevaluation can run.
challenge.resolution: Bootstrap locked candidate dependencies before Plan/Atlas.

challenge.scenario: A release unit legitimately modifies package.json and package-lock.json while current main still has the executor's previously installed dependency tree.
challenge.finding: Reusing the executor root node_modules would make Atlas and Plan load modules from the old main dependency graph, so a candidate could be semantically evaluated with packages or versions that are not declared by its own exact head.
challenge.resolution: Build the reevaluation environment from the candidate worktree itself with npm ci reading that candidate package-lock.json; never symlink or inherit root node_modules as reevaluation authority.

challenge.scenario: npm lifecycle scripts execute arbitrary candidate-controlled hooks.
challenge.finding: Proof environment would gain an unnecessary execution surface.
challenge.resolution: Use --ignore-scripts for reevaluation dependency bootstrap; if canonical tooling later proves a lifecycle-script dependency, address it explicitly rather than silently broadening authority.

challenge.scenario: The package registry is unavailable, lockfile integrity verification fails, or npm ci exits non-zero while preparing the isolated candidate worktree.
challenge.finding: Without a complete dependency graph the semantic Plan/Atlas result is unknowable; continuing to shoperation-plan-before-code.mjs would falsely convert missing prerequisite evidence into an authorization attempt.
challenge.resolution: Catch the bootstrap command failure inside reevaluateSuccessorManifest and return RELEASE_UNIT_SUCCESSOR_REEVALUATION_BLOCK with the installation error; do not invoke Plan, authorize the unit, mutate persisted state beyond the blocker, or create a child PR.

challenge.scenario: Executor job has write-capable GitHub token.
challenge.finding: Child npm/proof commands do not need repository mutation authority.
challenge.resolution: Override GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN to empty for bootstrap and Plan subprocesses.

challenge.scenario: Bootstrap passes but Plan detects true successor drift.
challenge.finding: Environment repair must not convert semantic BLOCK into PASS.
challenge.resolution: Keep existing Plan error handling and BLOCK contract unchanged.

challenge.scenario: Temporary worktree is removed after failure.
challenge.finding: Cleanup must not mask the authoritative blocker.
challenge.resolution: Return BLOCK inside try/catch and retain finally cleanup exactly as today.

challenge.scenario: Persisted U01 is already STALE from the live failure.
challenge.finding: Repair cannot manually rewrite authoritative state.
challenge.resolution: Merge the executor fix, then resume/reconcile only through canonical driver logic from persisted CAS state.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Implement dependency bootstrap in reevaluateSuccessorManifest and regression tests only.
Require exact-head Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, full tests, typecheck, build and Completion Truth PASS.
Commit only canonical lifecycle closure metadata and require final exact-head CI PASS.
Merge the fix, verify fresh main CI, then replay the unchanged multi-unit rehearsal from persisted CAS state without manual state edits.

requirements.requirement: Trusted release-unit reevaluation must establish the exact locked candidate dependency environment before semantic Plan/Atlas validation and must fail closed if that environment cannot be established.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Successor reevaluation may not execute semantic Plan/Atlas with unresolved declared dependencies.
Dependency/bootstrap and semantic proof subprocesses may not inherit repository write tokens.
